en.title: Agent Note: dsh-101 profile — a document-first learning surface for DSH
en.body:
# Agent Note: dsh-101 profile — a document-first learning surface for DSH

Status: proposed

## Problem

New users of DeepSeek Harness have no guided surface: the default web UI is a
session tree plus a chat composer, while the corpus of learning material
(READMEs, `docs/`, generated catalogs, `.agents/notes`, examples, skills,
profile templates) is scattered across the installation. There is no
navigation, no full-text search, no curated reading order, and no way for an
agent to answer questions *about DSH* with reliable citations back into the
docs.

## Proposal

Add a dedicated `dsh-101` profile (a bundle layer over `dsh-base` +
`dsh-web-app`) that provides a document-first reader UI while reusing the
existing session/model/theme/locale plumbing:

- **Corpus**: a build-time generator (`scripts/gen-dsh-101-corpus.ts`) scans
  the installation's markdown tree (repo root, `docs/`, `.agents/notes`,
  `examples/`, `skills/`, package READMEs) and emits a versioned JSON corpus
  (`index.json` + `documents/<id>.md`) into the `dsh-101` bundle package.
  Document ids are stable, derived from repository-relative paths (never from
  titles), so links survive renames of headings.
- **Content service** (`dsh-101-core`, host plugin `ctx.dsh101`): loads the
  corpus, provides read/search/status methods, and merges a user curation
  overlay (`$DSH_HOME/dsh-101/curation.json`) that carries module ordering,
  summaries, recommended reading order, best practices, and redirects —
  never document bodies. Search is a bounded in-memory index over title +
  section headings + paragraph text, with CJK-aware tokenization.
- **Reader UI** (`dsh-101-app`, dual-face plugin): registers the `root` slot
  with a three-column shell (module tree | article/home | collapsible tutor
  panel), deep-linkable article URLs (`/101/<locale>/<id>#<heading>`), module
  home page, full-text search view, and language-aware document display with a
  fallback notice when a locale variant is missing.
- **Tutor session** (`dsh-101-tutor`): sessions created from the reader carry
  a `dsh101` marker event; the plugin injects the current article context and
  exposes four model tools (`dsh101_search`, `dsh101_read`, `dsh101_open`,
  `dsh101_publish`). Answers render as citation cards that navigate the reader
  on click; explicit "open/take me to" language lets the agent navigate
  automatically. A "start building" handoff creates an ordinary coding session
  preloaded with the question, citations, and reading position.
- **Curation workflow**: on version mismatch the home page offers a
  one-click update that opens a curator session (a `dsh-101-curator` skill
  registered through `ctx.skills.register`). The agent inspects the new
  corpus and publishes a new `curation.json`; publishing is validated
  (schema, id coverage, link report, base revision) and atomic (temp file +
  rename), and failure keeps the previous overlay.
- **Model-less operation**: the corpus index, articles, navigation, and search
  all work with no LLM configured; the tutor panel shows a model-setup
  affordance instead.

The default `web` profile is untouched; `dsh-101` is a separate profile name.

## Acceptance criteria

- `dsh --profile dsh-101` boots with the reader UI; `dsh web` behavior is
  unchanged.
- The corpus generator is deterministic: running it twice yields identical
  output; ids are stable across title edits; zh/en pairs are detected and
  linked.
- Article read, module home, search, and deep links work with no API key.
- Curation overlay merges at runtime; publish is atomic and validated; a bad
  publish keeps the previous overlay and reports the error.
- Tutor sessions persist across article switches and reloads; citation cards
  and explicit navigation work; handoff creates an ordinary coding session.
- Unit tests cover id stability, i18n pairing, search, curation merge, and
  publish validation; the profile composes (dump-config includes the dsh-101
  rows and excludes the default UI rows).

## Risks

- **UI slot conflicts**: `dsh-101-app` registers the `root` slot, which the
  default `ui-layout` also registers; the profile patch must exclude the
  default UI rows, otherwise both roots render (or registration throws).
  Mitigation: bundle patch deletes the default client rows and the profile
  test asserts the composed list.
- **Corpus size**: a full installation has hundreds of markdown files;
  unbounded in-memory indexing is wasteful. Mitigation: index metadata plus
  bounded paragraph previews; document bodies are read on demand.
- **Search quality**: naive substring search over CJK text is weak.
  Mitigation: word-level tokenization with consecutive-run matching and
  title/heading weighting; accept v1 limits and document them.
- **Curator autonomy**: an agent-driven publish must not corrupt the overlay.
  Mitigation: schema validation, base-revision check, job-token gating, and
  atomic rename; the previous overlay is always recoverable.
- **Conversation embedding**: the reader's tutor panel embeds the existing
  conversation slot; if ui-conversation's layout assumptions conflict, v1
  falls back to a chat-in-drawer with the same session service.

## Alternatives considered

- **Add the reader into the default web UI** (rejected): the root slot is a
  single-occupant slot; injecting a second root would fight the default
  layout and change the product surface for every user. A separate profile
  keeps the blast radius zero.
- **Serve articles as static files through frontend-static** (rejected): the
  fallback seat is single-owner and serves one dist root; the article corpus
  is user-overlayable and needs the search index, so a plugin API is the
  right surface.
- **Extend the apiproxy RpcMethodMap with dsh101.\* methods** (rejected):
  the RPC map is a closed union owned by the host; a dedicated `/api/dsh101`
  prefix route on the webserver keeps the addition self-contained and HMR-
  friendly (same pattern as the connection plugin).
- **Store curation as full document copies** (rejected): copies drift from
  the versioned corpus; the overlay only carries ordering/summary/redirect
  metadata and falls back to the corpus content.
- **Do the curation at first run automatically** (rejected per product
  decision): automatic curation costs model calls and can fail silently; a
  home-page banner with a one-click action keeps the baseline deterministic.
